request_state.title: Baker-Wustholz Linear Forms in Logarithms on Semi-Abelian Varieties
request_state.text: Extend Baker effective logarithmic forms to semi-abelian varieties associated to A^x + B^y = C^z to bound max(x, y, z) independently of fixed bases.

relevance.instructions: How directly does this approach address the complete Beal conjecture across all three exponents x, y, z >= 3 simultaneously, rather than fixing two exponents?
criteria: level 0: fixes two or more exponents, reducing to a known single signature
level 1: handles one infinite family but requires fixing one exponent
level 2: operates on two independent exponents
level 3: applies to all three independent exponents x, y, z >= 3 under standard geometric/automorphic hypotheses
level 4: unconditionally proves the complete conjecture for all x, y, z >= 3

obstruction_risk.instructions: What is the risk of encountering an insurmountable barrier (e.g. non-effective Vojta, non-rigid higher rank monodromy, unbounded Selmer rank, or heuristic laundering)?
criteria: level 0: minimal risk; fully effective and proved tools exist
level 1: requires proving effective versions of known qualitative finiteness theorems
level 2: depends on deep unproved conjectures such as Vojta or Tate-Shafarevich finiteness
level 3: provably blocked by structural barriers (such as non-effective subspace theorem or failure of rank < genus)

recommended_action.instructions: What single next action should this candidate receive from the research loop right now?

criteria.formalize: the candidate argument is believed complete and small enough to check in Lean 4 or Z3
criteria.literature_check: the candidate next discriminating test is verifying a cited result against its primary source
criteria.park: the candidate may become useful later but nothing can discriminate it now, so it should be preserved untouched
criteria.discard: the candidate is refuted, duplicated, or has no path forward, and only its extracted lemma or obstruction is worth keeping
